method_card.title: Finding Missing Angles
steps: Name the setup: straight line (180°), point (360°), triangle (180°), quadrilateral (360°), or parallel lines.
Parallel lines: alternate and corresponding angles are equal; co-interior angles add to 180°.
Polygons: interior sum = (n − 2) × 180°; each exterior angle of a regular polygon = 360° ÷ n; interior + exterior = 180°.
Add what you know, subtract from the total (or solve the equation), then check it fits.
method_card.content:
Almost every angle problem shares out a known total. A straight line holds 180°, a point holds 360°, a triangle 180°, a quadrilateral 360°.

For an n-sided polygon the interior angles total \((n-2)\times 180°\); each exterior angle of a regular polygon is \(360°\div n\), and interior + exterior = 180°.
method_card.example:
Find each interior angle of a regular hexagon.

Sum \(= (6-2)\times 180 = 720°\); each \(= 720\div 6 = 120°\).

bronze.hint: Angles on a straight line add to 180, so subtract 72 from 180.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you used 360° for a straight line. A straight line is a half turn, 180°, so x = 180 − 72 = 108°.

guided_steps.say: The two angles sit on a straight line, which is a half turn.

guided_steps.pre: Angles on a straight line add up to
guided_steps.hint: A straight line is a half turn.

guided_steps.pre: Check they make a straight line: 108 + 72 =
guided_steps.done: That is a straight line, so x = 108° is right.

bronze.display: Vertically opposite angles: one is \(68°\). What is the other?
bronze.hint: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so the other is the same size.

misconceptions.message: You may have treated these as angles on a straight line. Vertically opposite angles are equal, not supplementary, so the other is 68°.

guided_steps.say: Two straight lines cross, making an X shape. The 68° angle and the one directly opposite are vertically opposite.

guided_steps.pre: Track it through the straight line first. The angle beside 68° is 180 − 68 =
guided_steps.hint: Angles on a straight line add to 180.

guided_steps.pre: The angle opposite 68° sits beside that 112° angle, also on a straight line: 180 − 112 =
guided_steps.done: That is why vertically opposite angles are always equal.

guided_steps.pre: Check all four fill the point: 68 + 112 + 68 + 112 =
guided_steps.hint: Angles at a point add to 360.
guided_steps.done: They fill the full turn, so the other angle is 68°.

bronze.hint: The three angles of a triangle add to 180.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you used 360° for the triangle. A triangle's angles add to 180°, so x = 180 − 40 − 75 = 65°.

guided_steps.say: All three angles of a triangle add to 180°.

guided_steps.done: That is a full triangle, so x = 65° is right.

bronze.display: Three angles at a point are \(90°\), \(145°\) and \(x°\). Find \(x\).
bronze.hint: Angles around a point add to 360.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you added the two known angles. They meet at a point (360°), so subtract: x = 360 − 90 − 145 = 125°.

guided_steps.say: These three angles meet at a single point and go all the way round, a full turn of 360°.

guided_steps.pre: Take that from the full turn: x = 360 − 235 =

guided_steps.done: A full turn, so x = 125° is right.

bronze.display: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Angle \(a\) is alternate to an angle of \(58°\). Angle \(b\) lies on a straight line with \(a\). Find \(b\).
bronze.hint: Alternate angles are equal, so find a first, then use the straight line for b.

misconceptions.message: That is angle a, the alternate angle, which is 58°. The question asks for b, which is on a straight line with a: b = 180 − 58 = 122°.

guided_steps.say: Two parallel lines with a transversal. Alternate angles (the Z shape) are equal.

guided_steps.pre: Angle a is alternate to 58°, so a =
Angle b is on a straight line with a, so b = 180 − 58 =
Check a and b make a straight line: 58 + 122 =
guided_steps.done: A straight line, so b = 122° is right.

bronze.display: Co-interior angles: one is \(110°\). Find the other.

misconceptions.message: You may have treated these as equal, like alternate angles. Co-interior angles add to 180°, so the other is 180 − 110 = 70°.

guided_steps.say: Co-interior angles (the C shape between parallel lines, on the same side) add up to 180°.

guided_steps.pre: Write the rule as a sum. The two angles total

guided_steps.done: They add to 180°, so the other is 70°.

bronze.display: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of \(70°\). Find the top angle.
bronze.hint: The two base angles are equal, and all three add to 180.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you subtracted only one base angle. An isosceles triangle has TWO equal base angles: top = 180 − 70 − 70 = 40°.

guided_steps.say: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles. Both are 70°.

guided_steps.pre: All three add to 180, so the top = 180 − 140 =

guided_steps.done: A full triangle, so the top is 40°.

bronze.display: A quadrilateral has angles \(80°\), \(100°\), \(95°\) and \(x°\). Find \(x\).
bronze.hint: The four angles of a quadrilateral add to 360.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you added the three known angles. A quadrilateral's angles add to 360°, so x = 360 − 275 = 85°.

guided_steps.say: The four angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°.

guided_steps.done: They add to 360°, so x = 85°.

silver.display: Find the interior angle sum of a nonagon (9 sides).

misconceptions.message: It looks like you multiplied 9 × 180. Subtract 2 from the number of sides first: (9 − 2) × 180 = 7 × 180 = 1260°.

guided_steps.say: The interior angle sum of a polygon is (n − 2) × 180°. A nonagon has n = 9.

guided_steps.hint: Take 2 off the number of sides.

guided_steps.pre: Check by splitting the nonagon into 7 triangles, each 180°: 7 × 180 =
guided_steps.done: A nonagon splits into 7 triangles, so 1260° is right.

silver.display: Find each interior angle of a regular hexagon.
silver.hint: Find the interior sum with (n − 2) × 180, then divide by 6.

misconceptions.message: 60° is the exterior angle (360 ÷ 6). The interior angle is 180 − 60 = 120°, or the interior sum 720 ÷ 6 = 120°.
720° is the total of all six angles. Divide by 6 for each one: 720 ÷ 6 = 120°.

guided_steps.say: A regular hexagon has 6 equal angles. Find the total, then share it out.

guided_steps.done: Six 120° angles total 720°, so each is 120°.

silver.display: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is \(40°\). How many sides?
silver.hint: Exterior angles add to 360, so divide 360 by the exterior angle.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you divided into 180°. The exterior angles add to a full turn, 360°, so n = 360 ÷ 40 = 9.

guided_steps.say: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°. Each one here is 40°.

guided_steps.done: Nine 40° exterior angles make 360°, so 9 sides.

silver.display: The interior angle of a regular polygon is \(156°\). Find the exterior angle.
silver.hint: Interior and exterior angles add to 180.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you subtracted from 360°. An interior and its exterior angle sit on a straight line and add to 180°, so exterior = 180 − 156 = 24°.

guided_steps.say: An interior angle and its exterior angle lie on a straight line, so they add to 180°.

guided_steps.pre: Check they make a straight line: 156 + 24 =
guided_steps.done: A straight line, so the exterior is 24°.

silver.display: Two angles in a triangle are \(3x°\) and \(5x°\). The third is \(44°\). Find \(x\).
silver.hint: Add all three angles, set the total to 180, then solve for x.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you left out the 44°. All three add to 180: 3x + 5x + 44 = 180, so 8x = 136 and x = 17.

guided_steps.say: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. Add the expressions and the number.

guided_steps.pre: The total is 180 and 44 is known, so 8x = 180 − 44 =

guided_steps.hint: Work out each angle and add.
guided_steps.done: The angles total 180°, so x = 17.

silver.display: The interior angle of a regular polygon is \(108°\). How many sides does it have?
silver.hint: Find the exterior angle (180 − interior), then divide 360 by it.

misconceptions.message: 72° is the exterior angle (180 − 108). The number of sides is 360 ÷ 72 = 5.

guided_steps.say: Work backwards. First the exterior angle, then how many fit into 360°.

guided_steps.pre: Check a regular pentagon: interior sum = (5 − 2) × 180 = 540, each = 540 ÷ 5 =
guided_steps.hint: Find each interior angle of a 5-sided shape.
guided_steps.done: Each interior angle is 108°, so 5 sides is right.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you added the four known angles. A pentagon's angles add to 540°, so x = 540 − 460 = 80°.

guided_steps.say: A pentagon has 5 angles that add up to (5 − 2) × 180 = 540°.

guided_steps.done: They total 540°, so x = 80°.

gold.display: A regular polygon has interior angle \(162°\). How many sides?
gold.hint: Find the exterior angle (180 − 162), then divide 360 by it.

misconceptions.message: 18° is the exterior angle (180 − 162). The number of sides is 360 ÷ 18 = 20.

guided_steps.say: From the interior angle, find the exterior, then see how many exterior angles fit into 360°.

guided_steps.done: Twenty 18° exterior angles make 360°, so 20 sides.

gold.display: In a parallelogram, one angle is \((3x + 10)°\) and the adjacent angle is \((2x + 20)°\). Find \(x\).
gold.hint: Adjacent angles in a parallelogram add to 180; form an equation and solve.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you set the two angles equal. Adjacent angles in a parallelogram add to 180°, not equal: (3x + 10) + (2x + 20) = 180, so 5x + 30 = 180 and x = 30.

guided_steps.say: Adjacent angles in a parallelogram (a co-interior pair) add to 180°. Add the two expressions.

guided_steps.hint: Work out both angles and add.
guided_steps.done: Adjacent angles add to 180°, so x = 30.

gold.display: The interior angles of a polygon sum to \(1620°\). How many sides does it have?

misconceptions.message: 9 comes from 1620 ÷ 180, but that equals n − 2, not n. Add 2 back: n = 9 + 2 = 11.

guided_steps.say: The interior angle sum is (n − 2) × 180°. Set it equal to 1620 and solve for n.

guided_steps.pre: That result is n − 2, so n = 9 + 2 =

guided_steps.hint: Put n = 11 back into the formula.
guided_steps.done: An 11-sided polygon has an interior sum of 1620°, so 11 sides.

gold.display: Two regular polygons share a side. One is a square and the other is a regular hexagon. Find the angle between the unshared sides at the shared vertex.
gold.hint: The three angles at the shared vertex fill 360; subtract the square and hexagon angles.

misconceptions.message: 210° is the square and hexagon angles added (90 + 120). The three angles at the vertex fill a full turn, so the gap = 360 − 210 = 150°.

guided_steps.say: At the shared vertex, three angles meet and fill a full turn of 360°: the square's angle, the hexagon's angle, and the gap.

guided_steps.pre: A regular hexagon's interior angle is (6 − 2) × 180 ÷ 6 =

guided_steps.done: The three angles make a full turn, so the gap is 150°.

gold.display: An exterior angle of a regular polygon is \(x°\). The interior angle is \(4x°\). Find \(x\).
gold.hint: Interior and exterior angles add to 180; use x + 4x = 180.

misconceptions.message: It looks like you used 360°. An interior and exterior angle sit on a straight line and add to 180°: x + 4x = 180, so 5x = 180 and x = 36.

guided_steps.say: An interior angle and its exterior angle add to 180° (a straight line). Here they are 4x and x.

guided_steps.done: They make a straight line, so x = 36.

problem_bank.bronze_description: One angle fact applied in a single step: straight lines, points, triangles, quadrilaterals and parallel-line angles.
problem_bank.silver_description: Polygon angle sums and regular-polygon angles, plus simple angle equations to solve.
problem_bank.gold_description: Work backwards from angle facts and combine several of them in one figure.

bronze.title: Bronze: one angle fact, one step
steps: Spot the setup: a straight line (angles add to 180°), a point (360°), a triangle (180°) or a quadrilateral (360°).
Parallel lines give equal angles: alternate (Z) and corresponding (F) are equal; co-interior (C) add to 180°. Vertically opposite angles are equal.
Add the angles you know, then subtract from the total to find the missing one.

example.question: Angles on a straight line are 130° and x°. Find x.

steps.label: Rule
steps.content: Angles on a straight line add to \(180°\).

silver.title: Silver: polygons and simple angle algebra
steps: Interior angle sum of an n-sided polygon = \((n-2) \times 180°\). For a regular polygon, divide that sum by n for each angle.
Exterior angles of any polygon add to 360°, so each exterior angle of a regular polygon = \(360° \div n\), and interior + exterior = 180°.
For angle algebra, add the expressions, set the total to 180° (triangle) or the correct polygon sum, then solve for the letter.

example.question: Find each interior angle of a regular pentagon.

gold.title: Gold: work backwards and combine facts
steps: Reverse the formulas: from an interior angle find the exterior (180 − interior), then \(n = 360 \div \text{exterior}\). From an angle sum, solve \((n-2) \times 180 = \text{sum}\).
Combine several facts in one figure: shared vertices, ratios of interior to exterior, or angle expressions that must add to a known total.
Always finish by checking your angle fits the rule you started from.

example.question: A regular polygon has exterior angle 24°. How many sides?

steps.say: You have probably heard skaters or gamers talk about pulling a '180' or a '360'. Those are angles, and you already know what they mean.

steps.pre: A '180' spins you to face the exact opposite way. A full spin, right back to where you started, is a '
steps.hint: A complete turn, all the way round.

steps.say: So a full turn is 360° and a half turn, facing the opposite way, is 180°. A straight line is exactly that half turn.

steps.pre: Two angles sit on a straight line. One is 120°. The line is a half turn (180°), so the other is 180 − 120 =
steps.hint: Both angles share the 180° of the half turn.

steps.say: That is the whole lesson in miniature: angles on a straight line share 180°, angles round a point share 360°, and nearly every fact here is one of those two turns split up. In algebra we call the missing angle \(x\) and write \(x + 120 = 180\).

bronze.display: A triangle has angles \(50°\), \(60°\) and \(x°\). Find \(x\).

steps.say: Every triangle's angles add up to 180°.

steps.pre: The angles of a triangle add up to

steps.done: A full triangle, so x = 70°. That is the one move: known angles subtracted from the total.

silver.display: Find each interior angle of a regular octagon.

steps.say: An octagon has 8 sides. Find the interior total, then share it between the 8 equal angles.

steps.hint: Two fewer than the number of sides.

steps.done: Eight 135° angles total 1080°, so each is 135°. The new move: find the sum, then divide.

gold.display: A regular polygon has interior angle \(150°\). How many sides?

steps.say: Work backwards. Turn the interior angle into an exterior angle, then count how many fit into 360°.

steps.done: Back to 150°, so 12 sides is right. The new move: reverse the formula to find n.
